newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Guinness sees tough markets.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Guinness sees tough markets.

text.p: British brewing and spirits group Guinness Plc turned in half year results above expectations on Thursday but chairman Tony Greener said markets in Europe were tough and not expected to change this year. "We would not expect that to change very much in the rest of the year," he told Reuters in an interview.

Guinness turned in pretax profits for the six months ending June 30 of 357 million pounds ($558.5 million), up from 340 million pounds previously and above expectations of 337 to 353 million. It paid out an interim dividend of 4.55 pence per share, up from 4.20 pence previously.

Greener said that overall, spirits prices were up 0.5 percent in the first half of the year to June 30 compared with the same period last year, but the full year effect would be a 2.0 percent increase on last year, he said.

He added that "on a round-the-world scan, we are actually rather pleased with the underlying performance in North America, in Latin America the overall position is quite encouraging, with Mexico and Venezuela difficult markets that are now stabilising."
